A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Stand-In, with matching authors, method and main experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout. v4 ends with references and omits v3's supplement; this is an observable document difference, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark comparisons, a 20-participant user study, component ablations and qualitative generation results in the main paper and supplement.

after.justification: v4 retains original quantitative comparisons, user-study results and ablations in Tables 1–3, together with qualitative experiments.

M1.justification: The conditional image branch, restricted self-attention, conditional position mapping, image-token LoRA and KV caching are unchanged. Removing supplementary Algorithm 1 removes documentation of the retained procedure, rather than establishing a method change.

E1.justification: The human-video training data and identity-preserving, non-human subject, pose-guided, stylization and face-swapping evaluations remain. Removed supplementary examples are additional instances within this coverage, rather than separately defined datasets, populations or tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain identical comparator membership. The omitted supplementary comparisons use the same Kling, ConsistID, Phantom-14B, Hunyuan-Custom and VACE-14B methods retained in Figure 8. The two newly cited talking-head works are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 5 changes the displayed conditioning prompt from a bouquet of pink-and-yellow blossoms to a more general bouquet/garden description, locally revising the reported qualitative test input. Training settings, evaluation metrics and the 20-participant, 10-video user-study design are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 5 revises the RSA attention-map illustration, and v4 removes much of Figure 18's supplementary multi-frame RSA/CPM evidence. Part of its female CPM example survives as v4 Figure 6. Both component tests and their quantitative evidence remain in Table 3, so the analytical scope changes modestly.

E5.justification: Both versions report aggregate benchmark and ablation scores and averaged user-study ratings. Neither provides repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests; the supplement adds no such reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain all numerical results, including Stand-In's 0.724 face similarity, 3.922 naturalness and 20.594 prompt-following score. Qualitative evidence changes: Figure 5 replaces attention maps and the VSA output, the original Figure 6 example disappears, and nonredundant supplementary comparisons and demonstrations in Figures 16–17 and 20–21 are omitted.

T1.justification: The coordinate definitions and attention equations (1)–(4) are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. The removed inference pseudocode restates the method rather than contributing a separate theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: lightweight identity control using approximately 1% additional parameters and 2,000 training pairs, strong comparative performance, and compatibility with other generation applications.

C2.justification: The explanations of RSA's static identity representation, CPM's positional separation and transfer to other applications remain. v4's 'stable proportions' wording reprises the facial-geometry interpretation already present in v3's supplementary Section 8. No substantive new interpretation or limitation is introduced.

D1.justification: v4 removes the supplementary inference pseudocode and the complete prompt documentation for main-paper comparisons, non-human generation, face swapping and generalization examples. This substantially reduces reproducibility documentation, although the printed repository link, preprocessing instructions, LoRA rank, hardware, training steps and batch size remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Ma et al.'s two-stage talking-head generation work and MagicTalk, appearing as v4 references 23 and 51. These are limited contextual additions; the positioning against face-encoder and full-finetuning approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The document loses its entire supplementary structure covering pseudocode, expanded comparisons, ablations, generalization and complete prompts. The main narrative changes little, with an added acknowledgment and small wording and cross-reference corrections. Figures 8 and 10 still direct readers to supplementary prompts absent from v4.

P2.justification: The supplementary Algorithm 1 display and Figures 14–21 disappear, substantially reducing the visual presentation. Some removed displays repeat main-paper content, and v4 Figure 6 reuses part of v3 Figure 18. Figure 5 replaces several panels and its prompt text; the main numerical tables retain their structure.

improvement.justification: The corrected Figure 5 cross-reference and added citations provide small benefits, but removing full prompts, pseudocode and nonredundant supplementary examples weakens reproducibility and scrutiny. Figures 8 and 10 retain references to the omitted supplement. The decline is limited because the method, numerical evidence and principal conclusions remain intact, and some removed displays were redundant.
